references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 14:15|Mark 14:15] gives the same description of the large, furnished upper room that the disciples were to find and prepare for the Passover meal.

In [ref:Matt 26:18-19|Matt 26:18-19], Jesus gives similar instructions to go to a specific man in the city to prepare the Passover meal, although details about the upper room are not explicitly mentioned here.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 22:8-11|Luke 22:8-11] shows that Jesus sends Peter and John ahead and tells them exactly what they will see—a man carrying a water jar—which leads them to the house where the room is located.

In [ref:Luk 22:13|Luke 22:13], the fulfillment of Jesus' words is confirmed: the disciples found everything just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal. This demonstrates Jesus' prophetic foreknowledge.

In [ref:Apg 1:13|Acts 1:13], an upper room (ἀνάγαιον/ὑπερῷον) is mentioned where the disciples gathered after Jesus' ascension. Tradition has linked this room to the same one used for the Last Supper.

In [ref:Apg 20:8|Acts 20:8], believers gather in an upper room (ὑπερῷον) for the breaking of bread, showing that early Christians continued to meet in such rooms, consistent with the pattern from Jesus' last meal.
